rationale: Both compile definitions into closures at definition time, use a map of stack-transforming functions, and handle case-insensitivity. A is more robust and better factored. Its tokenizer recognises ': ... ;' anywhere in a line, so it handles definitions mixed with other code or several on one line. B only accepts a definition that fills an entire line. A also moves body compilation into a documented compile function and parseNumber into its own helper, which keeps the main loop readable. B inlines the definition handling inside Forth. B has some good points: sentinel error variables, and shared stack-checking helpers. However, popOne and popTwo are misleadingly named, because they only peek and the callers then trim the stack manually. Overall A is clearer and handles more valid input.
